name: Macchiato
caffeine: All from the espresso; the spoonful of foam adds none, and a double carries about twice a single.

house.ask: Not printed on the menus: ask at lineup whether there is an espresso machine, whether the bar will make a macchiato on request, and the price.

what: A macchiato is an espresso marked with a spoonful of milk foam. The name is Italian for stained: the espresso is stained, not the milk. Bars often build it on a double; in Italy it is usually a single. The latte macchiato and the chain syrup drink are different things.
taste: Espresso with the sharp edge knocked off: a soft dairy note through the middle, a finish still clearly coffee.

steps: Pull a double, 18 to 20 g in, 36 to 40 g out, into a warmed demitasse.
While it pulls, stretch a little milk in the smallest jug to 140 to 150F (60 to 66C), silky, never stiff.
Let it settle, then spoon one dollop onto the middle of the shot.
Send it within thirty seconds and dump what is left in the jug.
make.ratio: A double marked with 0.5 to 1 oz of foam
make.dose: 18 to 20 g coffee; 0.5 to 1 oz milk
make.time: 25 to 30 second shot, out within thirty seconds

serve: On a saucer with a spoon, out inside thirty seconds so the mark is still a mark, not a cloud. Ask which macchiato the guest means first: the three come in different glasses.
story: Macchiato is Italian for stained or marked. In Italy it is the usual way to take milk after a meal, since a cappuccino belongs to the morning. The latte macchiato turns it over, and chain menus added a sweet third drink, so one word now orders three things.
guest: A macchiato is an espresso with a spoonful of foam on top, small and still clearly coffee. Is that the one you mean, or the tall latte macchiato?
watch: Ask which macchiato: the marked espresso, the tall latte macchiato, or the syrup drink from a chain menu.
A double with a full ounce of milk crowds a 2 oz cup; use the 3 oz demitasse.
The foam should be silky and wet, a visible mark, never a stiff dry cap.

recall.prompt: How is a macchiato made, and what goes in it?
recall.answer: A double, 18 to 20 g in and 36 to 40 g out, marked with one dollop of silky foam in a warmed 3 oz demitasse: espresso with its edge softened.

quiz.q: What does the Italian word macchiato mean, as the drink uses it?
quiz.explain: The espresso is marked with milk. Cortado means cut, ristretto restricted and lungo long.

quiz.q: How much milk goes onto a macchiato built on a double?
quiz.explain: One dollop of silky foam, sitting as a visible mark rather than stirring itself in.

quiz.q: Why might an Italian guest take a macchiato, not a cappuccino, after lunch?
options: A cappuccino is a morning drink
Bars stop steaming milk at noon
quiz.explain: In Italy the cappuccino belongs to the morning, so the macchiato is how milk is taken after a meal.
